title: Playtest notes — incremental tool telemetry and SDK handoff
content:
Context and goal:
This doc captures a quick playtest and synthesis of ideas for making incremental/streaming tool-calls observable and easy to reason about from the SDK developer's point-of-view. The primary goal: reduce cognitive friction when clients stitch hosted streaming AI responses with local/remote tool invocations, and provide minimal yet actionable telemetry for ops teams to detect regressions (latency, partial failures, fidelity loss).

Why this matters (real-world pain):
- Teams building compositional assistants (search + extractors + action runners) repeatedly hit three pain points: (1) no clear mapping between partial model output and tool invocation events, (2) opaque retry/fallback semantics when streams drop mid-tool-call, (3) sparse telemetry that forces full trace reconstruction.
- Ops requests: I need an answer to "Which tool call caused N+1 latency spikes in a given user session?" without reconstructing token-level logs offline.

Playtest summary (what we ran):
- Lightweight SDK changes (JS & Python) to attach a local event envelope to streaming frames.
- Backend: experimental flag stream_tool_envelope=true, produced compact markers in SSE/HTTP2 chunks: {frame_type, tool_id, tool_phase, seq, span_id}.
- End-to-end scenario: user asks clarifying Q -> model streams 'reasoning' frames -> SDK detects candidate tool call -> emits tool_call_start frame -> HTTP/2 stream continues while tool runs -> tool_call_end frame with result checksum.
- Observations: attaching phase markers improved developer debugging time dramatically in playtest (qualitative). However we saw slight overhead (~0.7ms/frame) and two edge cases that need product decisions (out-of-order frames when client-side batching enabled; and partial-tool failures where model continues to stream).

Design constraints and principles:
- Minimal mental model: SDK should surface a simple state machine for tool invocation: idle -> pending -> running -> completed | failed | aborted. Developer should not have to track raw token offsets.
- Backwards-compatible: markers must be opt-in and compressible; older clients should ignore unknown envelope fields.
- Low-overhead: prefer a compact envelope representation (single-byte tag + small ascii payload) to avoid token inflation and bandwidth blowup.
- Observable without logs leak: telemetry should not include PII or tool payloads; only non-sensitive metadata (tool_id hash, latency ms, phase transitions, non-sensitive error codes).

Proposal: compact stream-envelope + SDK primitives
1) Stream envelope (wire format):
- Each incremental chunk may be accompanied by an optional envelope header. The header is a short JSON or protobuf-lite with these fields: frame_type (reasoning|tool_event|final), tool_id (opaque id), tool_phase (start|ack|result|error), seq (monotonic per-session), span_id (trace-friendly). We propose base64-URL-encoded header prefixed with a single control byte 0x7E to avoid colliding with plain text.
- Example chunk (humanized):
  [0x7E]eyJmIjoidG9vbF9ldmVudCIsInQiOiJzdGFydCIsInQiZCI6IjEyMyJ9<NL>partial tokens...
  (SDKs will parse header and expose structured events to app code)

2) SDK surface (JS/Python) — ergonomic primitives:
- onStreamEvent(cb) -> cb receives {type: 'reasoning'|'tool_event'|'final', metadata: {...}, payload: 'delta text'}
- await callTool(toolDescriptor, opts) -> returns {status, resultSummary, telemetryId}. The SDK can automatically correlate a tool call with subsequent stream frames using seq/span_id.
- Optional: streamCheckpoint() returns a lightweight cursor that apps can store to resume from a logical point (not full token KV).

3) Telemetry events shipped to Console (non-PII):
- TOOL_CALL_START {telemetry_id, tool_id_hash, timestamp, session_id, model_version}
- TOOL_CALL_END {telemetry_id, latency_ms, result_code, session_id}
- STREAM_FRAME_DROP {session_id, seq, dropped_bytes, reason}
- STREAM_REORDER {session_id, seq_expected, seq_received}
Note: Provide sampling knobs; default 1% for detailed per-frame traces, higher for error events (100%).

Edge cases and open questions identified in playtest:
- Q1: When model continues streaming after a failed tool call, should SDK surface that as a merged stream or a separate branch? Two possible UXs:
  - Merge: app receives continued text in same onStreamEvent flow and needs to consult last tool telemetry to decide whether to trust the continuation. Pros: simpler API. Cons: hard to attribute content provenance.
  - Branch: SDK emits a branch marker and exposes a small DAG of partial outputs. Pros: clear provenance. Cons: higher mental load.
Recommendation: default to Merge but expose an opt-in branch mode via client config. Document the tradeoffs clearly in SDK guides.

- Q2: Out-of-order frames when client-side batching or network retries happen. Should the server reorder/hold frames until monotonic seq is satisfied? Holding increases tail-latency; reordering creates confusing debugging stories.
Recommendation: server should emit monotonic seq when possible; SDK should offer 'strictSequencing' flag for clients who want guaranteed ordering (SDK will buffer up to N ms before delivering). Default: best-effort ordering + reorder telemetry.

- Q3: Tool payload sensitivity. Some tool results are PII. Telemetry must never include payloads. Use hashed identifiers and result_code enums only. Provide opt-in hashed checksums for deduping but warn customers.

Mini spec: SDK example (JS, pseudo):

const client = Redwood.hosted('api-key', {streamToolEnvelope: true});
const s = await client.stream({prompt});

s.onStreamEvent(ev => {
  if (ev.type === 'tool_event' && ev.metadata.tool_phase === 'start') {
    // show spinner, lock UI region
  }
  if (ev.type === 'reasoning') {
    appendToTranscript(ev.payload);
  }
});

const res = await s.callTool({name: 'search', params}, {timeout: 4000});
// res.telemetryId can be queried in Console to see matching start/end entries

Operational checklist (for a pilot):
- Flag rollout: stream_tool_envelope=false by default. Gradual enable for internal orgs, then beta customers.
- Console: add a lightweight correlation view (session timeline) that can filter by telemetry_id and show start/end markers aligned with transcript snippets.
- SDK docs: write a short, pragmatic guide titled "How to debug tool-induced latency" with examples and common anti-patterns.
- Perf: measure overhead across 5ms, 10ms, 25ms p50 latency slices; ensure overhead <1% for typical chunk sizes.

Implementation plan and owner matrix (rough):
- Backend wiring + control plane flag: Marco Liu (eng-serving-runtime) — 2 sprints (include unit tests for seq monotonicity)
- SDK parsing and ergonomics (JS + Python): Sofia Green (developer-experience) — 3 sprints, include example apps
- Console timeline UI + telemetry ingestion: Devon Reyes (product-hosted-api + observability) — 4 sprints (simple view first)
- Security review: Priya Nair (security-and-compliance) — quick pass to confirm no payload leakage

Open action items (short):
- [Asha] Draft short API compatibility policy and publish in SDK repo (by 2025-06-30)
- [Marco] Prototype compact header encoding and measure bandwidth cost (by 2025-06-17)
- [Sofia] Implement onStreamEvent and callTool in JS SDK + sample app (by 2025-06-24)
- [Devon] Mock Console timeline and verify UX with 3 SREs (by 2025-07-08)

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider a 'tool confidence' hint from model (low/med/high) that can be emitted as part of reason frames. This helps UIs decide whether to surface a 'verify' button before calling expensive tools.
- Could reuse existing tracing/span ids to correlate telemetry; need to validate span sampling impact on backend storage costs.
- Offer a tiny server-side mode that will synthesize a minimal summary for replay when stream data is unavailable (for long-tail debugging).
